items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’m really talking Herbie particularly and McCoy particularly... as influences... Trane without McCoy? Sure, but really.

ctx.x: For example, at the end of ’65 McCoy Tyner and Elvin Jones left, because they couldn’t deal with the way the music was going. Did you ever talk to Elvin about this? Did he ever say anything?

No. It’s just what I read, what you read, that it was too loud, two drummers, and I think ego-wise, he didn’t want to be competing with anybody else. You know the way he was. And Rashied [Ali], he was the kid on the block. Who knows? McCoy couldn’t hear himself, he says.
But Elvin never said anything to you about this?
